newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end firm, but off highs.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end firm, but off highs.

text.p: Weakness on Wall Street and soggy U.S. Treasuries clipped some of the gains on the CAC index on Thursday, traders said.
Earlier, the blue chip index soared just over one percent, pulled by the expiry of March futures and options contracts.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 7.95 points or 0.3x percent at 2,656.68, while the CAC-40 futures contract was up 30.5 at 2,679.5 from Wednesday's close.

* Traders said there was no appetite to take big positions ahead of Easter market holidays on Friday and Monday. Markets appeared to have absorbed Tuesday's Fed funds' quarter percent rate rise to 5.50 percent.
Next Tuesday sees the U.S. National Association of Purchasing Management's (NAPM) March report and then Friday brings March payrolls data.

* Schneider ends up 0.41 percent. Insurer Axa-UAP said it sold 2.32 million shares in the electrical engineering company for a capital gain of 350 million francs. It will retain a seven percent stake.
* Seita, up 1.4 percent at 203.2, will ask shareholders' approval for a buy-back of 15 percent of the equity capital for a period of five years, to share out its 6.3 billion francs in cash.
* Pinault-Printemps jumps 5.13 percent to 2,420, cheering with a 30.6 percent net dividend rise to 32 francs.

* Suez retreats 0.38 percent to 290.9, while Lyonnaise des Eaux rises 1.59 percent to 575. The market views a reported merger deal by Lyonnaise on Suez, rather than a public share offer, will mean smaller rewards for Suez minorities.

* Lagardere, up 4.66 percent at 182, said it will place its intention to bid on Friday in the Thomson-CSF privatisation. Alcatel Alsthom, up 1.35 percent at 678, is also expected to bid. Firm and final bids are due by May 7.
* Canal Plus drops 5.15 percent to 1,106, on negative sentiment on the price paid in the Nethold merger.
